name: Instacart Market Basket Analysis 1st Place — F1-Optimal Reorder Set Prediction
summary: Two-stage pipeline computing rich user-product interaction features fed into a LightGBM reorder-probability model, followed by an exact dynamic programming algorithm (Faron's kernel) to select the product subset maximizing expected F1 score.
dejargonized_summary: Predict which grocery products a customer will reorder by first estimating the probability of each product being reordered using gradient boosting, then using a clever algorithm to pick the exact set of products that maximizes the F1 scoring metric.

inputs.name: order_history
inputs.constraints: Columns: user_id, product_id, order_number, day_of_week, hour_of_day, days_since_prior_order.

outputs.name: predicted_product_sets
outputs.constraints: Mapping from user_id to list of predicted reorder product_ids.

planning_constraints.subject: features_before_model
planning_constraints.statement: User-product aggregation and feature merging must precede the reorder probability model.
planning_constraints.rationale: LightGBM requires pre-computed feature vectors for each user-product candidate pair.

planning_constraints.subject: probabilities_before_dp
planning_constraints.statement: The reorder probability model must produce per-pair probabilities before F1 maximization DP.
planning_constraints.rationale: The DP algorithm takes calibrated probabilities as input to compute the optimal subset.

stages.name: User-Product Aggregation
stages.description: Compute historical reorder rates, day-of-week purchasing patterns, average days-since-prior-order, and other interaction statistics for every user-product pair.
stages.dejargonized_description: Calculate statistics about each customer's purchasing history for every product they have bought: how often they reorder it, which days they buy it, and how long between orders.

inputs.name: order_history
inputs.constraints: Full order history with user_id, product_id, order_number, day_of_week, hour, days_since_prior.

outputs.name: interaction_features
outputs.constraints: One row per user-product pair with aggregated statistics.

preconditions: Order history contains at least one prior order per user.
guarantees: Every historically ordered user-product pair has a feature row.

stages.name: Candidate Generation
stages.description: Filter to products each user has ordered at least once previously, forming the candidate set for reorder prediction.
stages.dejargonized_description: Only consider products the customer has bought before as potential reorders — do not predict completely new products.

outputs.name: candidate_pairs
outputs.constraints: Subset of user-product pairs that are candidates for reorder.

guarantees: Every candidate pair has at least one historical purchase.

stages.name: Feature Merging
stages.description: Join User-level features, Product-level features, and User-Product interaction features onto the candidate pairs to create the final training/inference feature matrix.
stages.dejargonized_description: Combine all the different types of statistics (about the customer, the product, and the customer-product relationship) into one table for the model to use.

outputs.name: feature_matrix
outputs.constraints: One row per candidate pair with all features joined.

preconditions: Candidate pairs and interaction features share user_id, product_id keys.
guarantees: All candidate pairs have complete feature vectors.

stages.name: Reorder Probability Model
stages.description: Train a LightGBM binary classifier to predict the probability that a user will reorder a given product in their next order.
stages.dejargonized_description: Use gradient-boosted decision trees to estimate how likely each product is to be reordered by the customer.

inputs.name: feature_matrix
inputs.constraints: Complete feature matrix for candidate pairs.

outputs.name: reorder_probabilities
outputs.constraints: Shape (N_candidates,): calibrated reorder probability per candidate pair.

preconditions: Feature matrix includes binary reorder target for training rows.
guarantees: Output probabilities are in [0, 1] for all candidate pairs.
family_notes: LightGBM chosen for speed and performance on large tabular datasets.

stages.name: F1 Maximization DP
stages.description: Run an exact dynamic programming algorithm (Faron's kernel) per user to select the product subset that maximizes the expected F1 score given individual reorder probabilities.
stages.dejargonized_description: Use a mathematical algorithm to pick the best set of products to predict for each customer, optimizing for the F1 score rather than just picking all products above a threshold.

inputs.name: reorder_probabilities
inputs.constraints: Per-candidate reorder probabilities for a single user, sorted descending.

outputs.name: predicted_product_sets
outputs.constraints: Mapping from user_id to optimal product subset.

preconditions: Probabilities are calibrated and per-user grouping is available.
guarantees: Selected subset maximizes expected F1 under the independence assumption.
family_notes: Implemented in custom Cython for performance.
KEY WINNING TECHNIQUE. Exact F1 optimization outperforms naive thresholding.
Based on the observation that F1 maximization over independent Bernoulli variables has an O(n^2) exact solution.

edges.provenance: Complete feature vectors for all candidate pairs.
Calibrated per-pair reorder probabilities for DP optimization.

audit.rationale: 1st place Kaggle Instacart Market Basket Analysis solution. Core innovation: exact DP for F1-optimal subset selection given per-item reorder probabilities from LightGBM.
audit.dejargonized_summary: Predict which products each customer will reorder by estimating individual reorder probabilities then mathematically selecting the best set to maximize the scoring metric.
provenance_notes: Source: Kaggle Instacart Market Basket Analysis competition, 1st place (2017)
uncertainty_notes: The independence assumption in F1 DP may not hold for complementary/substitute products.
Feature engineering details may vary from the exact 1st place implementation.
